title: Gene regulatory network inference in soybean upon infection by Phytophthora sojae
authors: Hale B; Ratnayake S; Flory A; Wijeratne R; Schmidt C; Robertson AE; Wijeratne AJ
one_liner_zh: 该文利用DAP-seq和深度学习预测大豆中WRKY/RAV转录因子的DNA结合位点并构建基因调控网络，虽聚焦植物免疫而非TF-DNA机制建模，但方法可迁移至TF-DNA互作研究。
abstract:
Phytophthora sojae is a soil-borne oomycete and the causal agent of Phytophthora root and stem rot (PRR) in soybean ( Glycine max [L.] Merrill). Yield losses attributed to P. sojae are devastating in disease-conducive environments, with global estimates surpassing 1.1 million tonnes annually. Historically, management of PRR has entailed host genetic resistance (both vertical and horizontal) complemented by disease-suppressive cultural practices (e.g., oomicide application). However, the vast expansion of complex and/or diverse P. sojae pathotypes necessitates developing novel technologies to attenuate PRR in field environments. Therefore, the objective of the present study was to couple high-throughput sequencing data and deep learning to elucidate molecular features in soybean following infection by P. sojae . In doing so, we generated transcriptomes to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs) during compatible and incompatible interactions with P. sojae and a mock inoculation. The expression data were then used to select two defense-related transcription factors (TFs) belonging to WRKY and RAV families. DNA Affinity Purification and sequencing (DAP-seq) data were obtained for each TF, providing putative DNA binding sites in the soybean genome. These bound sites were used to train Deep Neural Networks with convolutional and recurrent layers to predict new target sites of WRKY and RAV family members in the DEG set. Moreover, we leveraged publicly available Arabidopsis ( Arabidopsis thaliana ) DAP-seq data for five TF families enriched in our transcriptome analysis to train similar models. These Arabidopsis data-based models were used for cross-species TF binding site prediction on soybean. Finally, we created a gene regulatory network depicting TF-target gene interactions that orchestrate an immune response against P. sojae . Information herein provides novel insight into molecular plant-pathogen interaction and may prove useful in developing soybean cultivars with more durable resistance to P. sojae .

Author Summary

Global food security is threatened continually by plant pathogens. One approach to circumvent these disease-causing agents entails understanding how hosts balance primary growth and defense upon pathogen perception. Molecular signatures of perception-rendered defense may be leveraged subsequently to develop resistant/tolerant crop plants. Additionally, evidence suggests that the plant immune system is characterized by tuning primary and secondary metabolic activity via transcription factor-mediated transcriptional reprogramming. Therefore, we investigated transcription factor-target gene interactions in soybean upon infection by compatible and incompatible races of Phytophthora sojae . Through transcriptome analysis, we found that the interactions elicited vast, overlapping transcriptional responses and identified overrepresented, defense-related transcription factor families. We then generated/acquired DNA-protein interactome data for the most represented transcription factor families in the transcriptome analysis and trained deep learning-based models to predict novel transcription factor targets. Transcription factor/target gene metrics were used to construct a gene regulatory network with prioritized components. We identified hub transcription factors belonging to WRKY and ERF families, the majority of which function in response to various biotic and abiotic stressors. These findings propose novel regulators in the soybean defense response to Phytophthora sojae and provide an avenue for the investigation of transcription factor-target gene interactions in plants.
abstract_zh:
大豆疫霉（*Phytophthora sojae*）是一种土传卵菌，是大豆（*Glycine max* [L.] Merrill）疫霉根腐病（PhR）的病原体。在有利于病害发生的环境中，由大豆疫霉造成的产量损失极为严重，全球年损失估计超过110万吨。历史上，疫霉根腐病的治理主要依靠寄主遗传抗性（包括垂直抗性和水平抗性），并辅以抑制病害的栽培措施（如施用杀卵菌剂）。然而，复杂和/或多样化的大豆疫霉致病型的广泛扩展，迫切需要开发新技术以在田间环境中减轻疫霉根腐病。因此，本研究的目标是将高通量测序数据与深度学习相结合，以阐明大豆受大豆疫霉侵染后的分子特征。为此，我们生成了转录组，以鉴定在与大豆疫霉亲和性和非亲和性互作及模拟接种过程中的差异表达基因（DEGs）。随后，利用表达数据筛选出两个属于WRKY和RAV家族的防御相关转录因子（TFs）。获得了每个转录因子的DNA亲和纯化测序（DAP-seq）数据，提供了大豆基因组中的推定DNA结合位点。这些结合位点被用于训练具有卷积层和循环层的深度神经网络，以预测DEG集合中WRKY和RAV家族成员的新靶位点。此外，我们利用公开的拟南芥（*Arabidopsis thaliana*）DAP-seq数据，针对转录组分析中富集的五个转录因子家族训练了类似模型。这些基于拟南芥数据的模型被用于大豆上的跨物种转录因子结合位点预测。最后，我们构建了一个基因调控网络，描绘了协调针对大豆疫霉免疫应答的转录因子-靶基因相互作用。本文提供的信息为分子植物-病原体互作提供了新见解，并可能有助于开发对大豆疫霉具有更持久抗性的大豆品种。

作者总结

全球粮食安全持续受到植物病原体的威胁。规避这些致病因子的一种方法在于理解寄主在感知病原体后如何平衡初级生长与防御。感知引发的防御的分子特征随后可用于开发抗病/耐病作物。此外，有证据表明，植物免疫系统的特征在于通过转录因子介导的转录重编程来调节初级和次级代谢活动。因此，我们研究了大豆在受亲和性和非亲和性大豆疫霉生理小种侵染时转录因子-靶基因的相互作用。通过转录组分析，我们发现这些互作引发了广泛且重叠的转录响应，并鉴定了过表达的防御相关转录因子家族。随后，我们生成/获取了转录组分析中代表性最高转录因子家族的DNA-蛋白质互作组数据，并训练了基于深度学习的模型以预测新的转录因子靶标。利用转录因子/靶基因指标构建了一个具有优先组分的基因调控网络。我们鉴定了属于WRKY和ERF家族的枢纽转录因子，其中大多数在响应各种生物和非生物胁迫中发挥作用。这些发现提出了大豆对大豆疫霉防御反应中的新型调控因子，并为研究植物中转录因子-靶基因相互作用提供了途径。
